note: Ada now heard Finn snoring only from two, so nothing rules Finn out for the hour from one, while the causeway was dry.

patch.value: From one until three, Finn snored on my sofa, right outside my bedroom door. I heard the clock chime one, two and three. He never stopped once!
From two until three, Finn snored on my sofa, right outside my bedroom door. I heard the clock chime two and three. Before that I was fast asleep!
I was in bed in my cottage from midnight until four. I hardly slept a wink.
I was in bed in my cottage from midnight until four. I slept a little, then lay awake listening to Finn snore.

Roz Pike, the village lamp-maker, took the lighthouse lens. Yesterday just after lunch, while Keeper Ada fetched water, Roz changed Ada's tide schedule so last night's low tide read 5 a.m. instead of 2 a.m. That made Ada set her alarm for four, so she was not watching the causeway at the real low tide. Between about 1 and 3 a.m., while the causeway was dry, Roz pushed her handcart over, took the lens and wheeled it back to hide in her shop. A scrap of the cradle's blue velvet caught on the quay railing. Finn, asleep on Ada's sofa, snored all night and kept Ada awake, so he never crossed. His round bundle is only a birthday sign for Ada.
